$comment: Every constant that more than one runtime needs, once (OI-NPPS-CORE-01). `bun scripts/sync-constants.ts` writes them into common/lib/constants.generated.ts, NppsConstants.generated.kt (Android), NppsConstants.generated.swift (iOS), NppsConstants.generated.cs (Windows) and common/npps-ffi/include/neurone_npps_status.h and firmware/common/include/np_app_wire_constants.h (the hub's side of the BLE contract), and --check fails if one is stale; the Rust core takes them at build time (common/npps-core/build.rs), so it has no copy to go stale. A constant is UPPER_SNAKE_CASE and has the SAME spelling in every language: that is the name, not a per-language rendering of it. The group (`name`) is the container where a language has one (`NPHardwareLimits.PBM_DEEP_MAX_MW_CM2`); `rust` is its module and `cPrefix` the prefix C needs because it has no namespaces. `targets` says which languages get a group, and `intTypes` overrides (a constant's own `types` overrides one for it alone; `hex` writes it in hex; `cName` is the full C macro name where it is not the group's prefix plus the name; a `value` that is a string makes a string constant) the type a language gives its whole numbers (the validator compares in f64, as JavaScript does, and the C ABI's codes are Rust i32 and Swift Int32, because that is what the calls return). `int` marks a whole-number figure. A group with a `uuidBase` is a table of 16-bit BLE ids: it also generates the 128-bit UUID strings (GattIds -> GattUuidStrings), and its constants marked `hub` are the ones the hub firmware publishes. `firmwareHeader` puts a C group into np_app_wire_constants.h; `hexWidth` writes a group's ids in hex. Provenance is in each note.

groups.name: NPHardwareLimits
groups.note: Every hardware ceiling and fixed device figure the apps and the shared validator use. The firmware enforces them independently; no dosage limit or clinician override can exceed them.

constants.note: PBM Transcranial / Intranasal (shared firmware limit)

constants.name: PBM_PULSED_PEAK_MW_CM2
constants.note: pending RISK-03 regulatory opinion

constants.name: PBM_DEEP_MAX_MW_CM2
constants.note: Deep 1170 nm PBM ceiling (CLAUDE.md §3: ≤1,000 mW/cm², TEC-stabilised).

constants.name: PBM_AGGREGATE_MAX_MW_CM2
constants.note: Aggregate PBM irradiance ceiling (OI-PBM-05, three-channel combined). Pending RISK-03 regulatory opinion scope expansion (Q4–Q6).

constants.name: BES_TACS_MAX_MILLIAMPS
constants.note: BES / tACS (consumer: Brainwave Entrainment Stimulation)

constants.name: TDCS_MIN_MILLIAMPS
constants.note: tDCS (consumer: Cortical Priming Stimulation)

constants.name: TDCS_MAX_SESSION_CHARGE_DENSITY_MC_CM2
constants.note: OI-CHARGE-04 (closed 2026-09-09): this IS checked here now. There is no web electrode-area constant to add, because there is no longer a global electrode area on any client — the area is authored per protocol (TDCSParams.electrodeAreaCm2), travels in the signed session descriptor, and the safety MCU derives its charge limit from that same declared number. What used to be a 35-vs-25 disagreement between the app's assumption and the enforcer's is now one transmitted value. OI-CHARGE-05 (a)(d) 2026-09-15: RENAMED AND RE-SOURCED. This used to be `tdcsMaxChargeDensityUCcm2: 40.0`, a misnomer that concealed a 1000× divergence — `I(mA) × t(s) / A(cm²)` is mC/cm², so the clients enforced 40 mC/cm² while the safety MCU enforced 40 µC/cm². The name now states the unit AND the period, because both were ambiguous and each hid a different defect: the unit hid the 1000×, and the missing period hid that a per-phase pulsed figure was being applied to a DC session dose. 150 mC/cm² per session per electrode, derived rather than asserted (the old 40 had no source anywhere in the tree — the citation chain was circular). Bounds the conventional large-pad human tDCS envelope: the most-exposed large RCT protocol in docs/tdcs_database_full.csv is Brunoni ELECT-TDCS 2013/2017 at 2 mA × 30 min on 25 cm² = 144 mC/cm². Margin check: 35× below Liebetanz 2009's measured rat epicranial DC lesion threshold of 5,240 mC/cm². Full derivation: NP-DT-001 DI-SAFE-01.

constants.name: PULSED_MAX_PHASE_CHARGE_DENSITY_UC_CM2
constants.note: Per-PHASE ceiling for the charge-balanced biphasic modalities — BES/tACS, VNS, cervical VNS, clinical tACS (OI-CHARGE-05 (b)). 40 µC/cm² is a real and correct figure in this form (Shannon 1992 / McCreery 1990 pulsed charge-injection limits); it is the number the tree has always carried, now applied to the waveform class it is actually about. Net charge on these modalities is ~zero by construction, so a session-cumulative dose is not a physical quantity for them and is not checked.

constants.name: BES_ELECTRODE_AREA_CM2
constants.note: Electrode areas for the modalities whose electrodes are FIXED PARTS OF THE PRODUCT rather than a user-chosen consumable. The tDCS pad is authored per protocol precisely because the user picks it (OI-CHARGE-04); the BES pads, auricular clip and cervical collar are not swappable, so their area is a device property both the app and firmware may hold. ⚠ PROVISIONAL — NOT MEASURED (OI-CHARGE-07). Mirrors firmware/hub_control/include/np_hub_config.h. A SMALLER area is a SMALLER charge budget, so these may be revised down freely and may only be revised up against a measurement.

constants.name: VNS_DEFAULT_PULSE_WIDTH_SECONDS
constants.note: Pulse width (seconds) the firmware substitutes when a descriptor declares none: np_mod_cvns.c and np_session_runner.c both default to 250 µs. The pre-flight must use the same number or it validates a different waveform than the one that runs.

constants.name: TDCS_MAX_ELECTRODE_AREA_CM2
constants.note: Largest declarable per-electrode area: the wire field (np_mod_tdcs_params_t.electrode_area_mcm2) is a uint16 of milli-cm², so 65535 mcm². Not a clinical limit — an encoding ceiling, well above any real pad (a large sponge is 35 cm²).

constants.name: TDCS_DEFAULT_ELECTRODE_AREA_CM2
constants.note: What a NEW tDCS block is seeded with in an editor (a large sponge pad). It is not a limit: the area is authored per protocol, travels in the signed descriptor, and the safety MCU derives its charge limit from that declared number (OI-CHARGE-04).

groups.name: NppsStatus
groups.note: Return codes of the shared core's C ABI (common/npps-ffi/include/neurone_npps.h). A refusal (1) and an internal error (2) carry a UTF-8 message in the output buffer; a bad argument (3) carries none.

constants.name: OK
constants.note: Success: the output buffer holds the result.

constants.name: REFUSED
constants.note: The core refused the input; the buffer holds the refusal message.

constants.name: INTERNAL_ERROR
constants.note: The core panicked; the buffer holds a message.

constants.name: BAD_ARGUMENT
constants.note: A null pointer or non-UTF-8 input; no buffer.

groups.name: GattIds
groups.note: The 16-bit id of each characteristic (every name ends in _ID, so SESSION_STATE_ID is never mistaken for the session state itself) of the NeurOne BLE service. The 128-bit UUID is the base with its second group replaced by the id (4E455550-XXXX-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB), so the base is written once, here, and every runtime builds its UUIDs from it. `hub: true` marks a characteristic the hub firmware publishes; only those reach the firmware header, because a firmware reference is what the consumable-trigger gate reads as 'the hub produces it'. `required: true` marks the characteristics an app must find before it treats a hub as fully resolved; the others are optional, or T2 only, or not yet published (OI-WA-03).

groups.note: The anonymisation floors a study descriptor must meet before a user may be asked to consent to it (CLAUDE.md §5.3, §6.3). Locked; the device is the only place they can be enforced, because the anonymisation happens on the device.

constants.name: MINIMUM_K_ANONYMITY
constants.note: A descriptor's k must be at least this.

constants.name: MINIMUM_DATE_ROUNDING_DAYS
constants.note: A descriptor's date rounding must be at least this many days (one week).

groups.name: CvfsWire
groups.note: The CVNS_FAULT_STATUS frame (NP-SW-FAULTMSG-001): a 4-byte header then up to MAX_WIRE_RECORDS records of RECORD_LEN bytes. The hub writes it and the apps parse it.

constants.name: WIRE_VERSION
constants.note: Byte 0 of the frame.

constants.name: HEADER_LEN
constants.note: Header bytes before the first record.

constants.name: RECORD_LEN
constants.note: Bytes in one fault record.

constants.name: MAX_WIRE_RECORDS
constants.note: Most records one frame carries.

groups.name: ZoneNotify
groups.note: The ZONE_MODULE_STATUS notification frame (np_zone_notify.h): a 4-byte header then fixed-size records, either status records or socket-map records. The hub writes it and both apps parse it. Version 2 is the static/dynamic split: status records dropped from 4 to 3 bytes when anatomy moved into the socket map. Version 1 (anatomy inline on every change) was never deployed, and version 0 was the retired 5-byte payload with no version byte, so a hub still speaking it decodes as 0 and is rejected rather than misread.

constants.name: FORMAT_VERSION
constants.note: Byte 0 of every frame.

constants.name: HEADER_BYTES
constants.note: Header bytes before the first record: byte 0 format version, byte 1 flags (including the frame kind bit), byte 2 fragment index (0-based), byte 3 record count in this fragment.

constants.name: STATUS_REC_BYTES
constants.note: Status record: socket id (1-based), module type, flags.

constants.name: MAP_REC_BYTES
constants.note: Map record: socket id (1-based), flags, then x_mm, y_mm, z_mm as int16 little-endian.

constants.name: MAX_SOCKET_ID
constants.note: Largest 1-based socket id the wire can carry. Firmware ids are 0-based over NP_HEXMAP_MAX_SOCKETS (128), so the 1-based domain is 1..128, exactly a uint8_t's usable range above zero. Pinned by a static assert in np_zone_notify.c against NP_HEXMAP_MAX_SOCKETS.

constants.name: FLAG_SNAPSHOT
constants.note: Frame flag (byte 1): this fragment belongs to a full snapshot. Clear = incremental delta naming only the sockets that changed. Socket-map frames are always snapshots.

constants.name: FLAG_LAST
constants.note: Frame flag (byte 1): final fragment of this frame sequence. A snapshot is committed by the app only when a fragment carrying this flag arrives.

constants.name: FLAG_MAP
constants.note: Frame flag (byte 1), the frame KIND: set = socket-map records, clear = status records. The two shapes differ in size, so a decoder that assumed the wrong one would misparse rather than fail; the kind is on the wire so it can be checked, not inferred from which characteristic delivered it.

constants.name: REC_PRESENT
constants.note: Status-record flag (record byte 2): a module is seated and confirmed in this socket. Clear = socket is empty (a removal, or an empty socket in a snapshot).

constants.name: REC_FAULT
constants.note: Status-record flag (record byte 2): the module failed identification (unrecognised type, bad contact, failed debounce). PRESENT is clear whenever FAULT is set: an unidentified module is never reported as usable.

constants.name: MAP_WIRED
constants.note: Map-record flag (record byte 1): this socket is physically wired in this shell. Clear = the address exists in the geometry table but the shell does not populate it.

groups.name: HubDescriptorWire
groups.note: Sizes and flags of the signed session descriptor the apps build and the hub verifies (NP-FW-HUB-001 §4).

constants.name: UUID_LEN
constants.note: The session UUID, the UHDR key.

constants.name: SIG_LEN
constants.note: The Ed25519 signature at the end of the blob.

constants.name: FLAG_T2_TIER
constants.note: Descriptor flag bit 0, computed by the app. It carries no authority: no firmware decision reads it, because whether a protocol is T2 comes from its modality set and whether this unit may run one is the safety MCU's signed tier identity (RISK-PWRSRC-10).

groups.name: BleTransfer
groups.note: Sizes of the BLE writes the apps make: the Mode 2 protocol upload and the OTA image. Both apps chunk to these.

constants.name: MAX_WRITE_SIZE
constants.note: The BLE 5 ATT MTU write ceiling, in bytes.

constants.name: MAX_CHUNK_PAYLOAD
constants.note: The most a START chunk carries (512 − 1 header − 2 length); also the single-chunk threshold.

constants.name: MAX_CONT_PAYLOAD
constants.note: The most a CONT or END chunk carries (512 − 1 header).

constants.name: OTA_CHUNK_SIZE
constants.note: ATT_MTU(512) − 3 ATT header − 1 OTA opcode − 2 chunk index leaves 506; 496 keeps a margin for GATT stack overhead.

constants.name: CVNS_ELECTRODE_COUNT
constants.note: Pads checked every session: the bilateral gel-pad assembly, left and right.

groups.name: PersistedKeys
groups.note: Storage keys and tags both apps use, written once so iOS (UserDefaults) and Android (the key-value store) cannot drift apart.

constants.name: ENROLMENT_KEY
constants.note: Characterisation enrolment flag. Distinct from WARRANTY_CONSENT_KEY by design: a shared key would make the two consents one consent.

constants.name: CONSENT_EPOCH_KEY
constants.note: Consent generation. Incremented on every grant, never reset by withdrawal. It travels with each uploaded record so a row cannot outlive the grant that authorised it: a device that withdrew and later re-enrolled produces records under a new epoch, and rows from the old one are identifiable for deletion without needing a clock to order them.

constants.name: PROGRAMME_ID_KEY
constants.note: The programme this device is enrolled in. Consent to programme N does not authorise programme N+1; the firmware rejects a mismatch and emits a standard-only record.

constants.name: CURRENT_PROGRAMME_ID
constants.note: Current programme generation. A new programme takes a new id and requires fresh enrolment; it does not inherit this one's participants.

constants.name: RESEARCH_ANALYTICS_KEY
constants.note: Set when the user actively completes the consent onboarding flow (taps Done on the final layer). Distinct from np.onboarding.consent-shown, which is set when the view appears. Not set when the user presses Skip, because skipping defers all data decisions including research analytics. Cleared by blanket research consent withdrawal, because blanket withdrawal implies full data-collection opt-out. Not the same as the warranty consent key: research and warranty consent are independent and must never share a key.

constants.name: CERVICAL_FAULT_LEDGER_KEY
constants.note: Prefix of the per-user key recording the last acknowledged cervical fault session.

constants.name: CONSUMABLE_RESET_KEY
constants.note: Consumable replacements waiting for the hub to acknowledge.

constants.name: SNOOZE_KEY
constants.note: Per-consumable reminder snooze counts.

constants.name: PARTICIPATION_KEY
constants.note: Study participations the user has joined.

constants.name: RESEARCH_SUGGESTIONS_KEY
constants.note: Locally stored research suggestions.

constants.name: SESSION_HISTORY_KEY
constants.note: The on-device session history.

constants.name: FIRST_SETUP_KEY
constants.note: The first hardware setup has completed.

constants.name: AGE_CONFIRMED_KEY
constants.note: Persists age-gate completion (ISC-87).

constants.name: STUDY_DESCRIPTOR_VERSION
constants.note: Domain-separation tag at the head of the canonical form a study descriptor is signed over.
